title: Getty Family and Koch to Take Over Getty Images in $533M Bankruptcy Deal
summary:
Public shareholders in Getty Images will be wiped out under a Chapter 11 bankruptcy plan that transitions the visual content company to private ownership. The prepackaged filing involves a restructuring support agreement where the Getty and Koch families will provide a capital injection in exchange for 100% of the company. As part of the deal, Getty will retire $270 million in unsecured notes and grant secured lenders longer maturities and lower interest rates.

The reorganization follows the accumulation of $2.1 billion in debt and a 25% drop in annual subscribers, which fell to 240,000 from 321,000 in one year as AI-generated imagery reduced demand for stock photography. For the second quarter ending June 30, the company reported $51.6 million in cash and negative free cash flow of $122.6 million. The filing comes four years after Getty was valued at $4.8 billion in a SPAC IPO and follows the July failure of a proposed $3.7 billion merger with Shutterstock.

selectedTweets.text:
AI + Debt destroys Getty Images, files for bankruptcy today 4 years after valued at $4.8 Billion in SPAC IPO:

Public shareholders get $0.

By most measures the business itself was fine:
• ~$910M revenue run-rate • 27% adjusted EBITDA margins • 59% of revenue on annual subscriptions • Editorial revenue up 9% last quarter

It was the debt and AI churn on consumer side of business that sank it.

At June 30:
 • $2.1B of debt • ~$250M of annualized adjusted EBITDA (Q2 x 4) • $51.6M of cash • Negative $122.6M of free cash flow in Q2

That works out to about 8x leverage on revenue that was down 4% in constant currency.

At 8x, the plan only works if everything goes right. 

Instead:

• AI took the low end. Annual subscribers fell from 321K to 240K in a year, a 25% drop. • Subscription revenue retention fell from 93.4% to 88.4%. • The plan to fix the balance sheet was a $3.7B merger with Shutterstock. UK regulators required a sale of Shutterstock's editorial business. Getty walked away in July after spending more than $100M on the deal.

Three months later Getty signed the restructuring. The Getty family and Koch are putting in up to $533M and will own 100% of the company. $270M of unsecured notes get retired, and secured lenders get lower rates and longer maturities.

8x leverage can work when revenue is growing 10%. Getty's revenue was shrinking and its retention was falling, and a 27% margin couldn't cover that gap.

If you have venture debt or any other loan, track two numbers: debt as a multiple of real cash flow, and what that multiple becomes if AI takes your low end the way it took Getty's.
